page: Amazon Web Services m7i.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz, providing 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, translating to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reveal strong single-core capabilities, with Geekbench single-core scoring 2025.0 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 32.15 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show some limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and large-block memory read bandwidth fall into the lower tier, while static web serving throughput remains moderate at 7.9 GB/sec. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for deep learning and cryptography acceleration.

From a resource-density perspective, the m7i.xlarge offers a balanced general-purpose profile suitable for workloads that benefit from strong single-threaded performance but do not require heavy multi-core scaling or high-speed local storage. It is well-suited for applications such as lightweight web serving, text processing, and basic single-threaded data manipulation. It is less optimal for heavy database operations or multi-threaded compilation tasks due to lower relative multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmark results.
